text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein inspects royal armed mechanical division.
- Foreign Minister Tarawnah calls for the relaunch of the Middle East peace process and urges the U.S. to play the role of full partner.
- Opposition deputies demand an extraordinary session of parliament to discuss a spate of temporary laws issued recently by the government which they say bypasses the role of parliament.
- Lawyer of Jordanian soldier who shot dead Israeli schoolgirls says his trial starts next Tuesday; defence wants to expand legal team defending the soldier.
- Parliamentary deputies start a campaign of signatures to convene an extraordinary session of parliament.
- Crown Prince Hassan discusses in London with British Foreign Minister Robin Cook the European role in the peace process.
- Water minister says pollution is behind a temporary stoppage in water supplies to the Baqaa Palestinian refugee camp.

- Professional unions decide mass resignations within a month if the government does not rescind the press and publications law in a move escalating the confrontion with the government against the new press and publications law.
- Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali begins a tour of the southern governates.
- Jordanian ambassador in Cairo says Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak to visit Jordan soon.
- Israel makes allegations of property ownership in Jordan going back to the 1920's.
- Agro-businesses in the south want clarifications on government policy towards buying the 1997 wheat and corn harvest.
